catalog_entry.title: Pairwise Relational Baseline
catalog_entry.summary: A pairwise comparison pack that centers attachment, relational care signaling, and broad trait scaffold without collapsing them into one score.
catalog_entry.notes: This is a disciplined baseline for pairwise or relationship-oriented work. It emphasizes regulation, care signaling, and broad trait context while keeping unsupported relational claims visible.

protocol.name: Pairwise Relational Comparison
protocol.purpose: Compare two subject stacks side by side without collapsing convergence, friction, orthogonality, and missingness into one compatibility score.
protocol.summary: A comparison program for pairwise or relationship-adjacent work that uses translation, paradox preservation, and evidence bracketing to keep relational claims scoped to what the inputs can actually support.
required_inputs: two explicitly separated stacks or structured result bundles
framework records for any compared systems
declared comparison question or relationship context
protocol.notes: This program is for disciplined pairwise comparison, not deterministic compatibility scoring. It should preserve asymmetry and leave unsupported seams visible.

techniques.name: Cross-Framework Translation
techniques.purpose: Translate constructs across systems without forcing false equivalence.
techniques.summary: Compare constructs through shared motifs, relationship semantics, and epistemic bracketing rather than by naive one-to-one conversion.
steps: Identify source and target layers of personhood.
Compare through shared motifs before direct translation.
Mark overlap as strong, partial, inverse, symbolic, or incommensurable.
cautions: Do not flatten symbolic and psychometric systems into one evidence bucket.
Preserve asymmetry when one framework is broader or socially different than the other.

techniques.name: Paradox Scan
techniques.purpose: Surface load-bearing contradictions rather than averaging them away.
techniques.summary: Detect tensions across frameworks, constructs, and observations that may indicate adaptation, context splits, or multi-layer organization.
steps: Check whether the signals operate on different layers.
Preserve contradiction when it remains explanatorily useful.
cautions: Do not turn every mismatch into pathology.

techniques.name: Contradiction Preservation
techniques.purpose: Keep the system from over-compressing a person or a framework into false coherence.
techniques.summary: Treat unresolved conflict, multiplicity, and context-dependence as data instead of noise to be smoothed out.
steps: Delay forced synthesis until one reading clearly dominates.
cautions: Avoid rhetorical neatness when the material is genuinely split.

techniques.name: Symbolic vs Empirical Bracketing
techniques.purpose: Use symbolic systems without pretending they carry the same evidence type as psychometrics.
techniques.summary: Distinguish descriptive usefulness, symbolic resonance, and empirical status so that heterogeneous frameworks can coexist in one map.
steps: State its social or symbolic usefulness separately.
Preserve both without collapsing either into the other.
cautions: Inclusion in the map does not imply equal evidence.

component_programs.name: Translation Memo
component_programs.purpose: Generate an evidence-aware memo about overlap, divergence, and incommensurability between selected frameworks or constructs.
component_programs.summary: A compact comparative program for agents that need to explain how two or more systems connect without forcing a single unified language.
component_programs.notes: Translation memos are useful baseline artifacts for both curation and downstream synthesis.

component_programs.name: Paradox Finder
component_programs.purpose: Surface load-bearing contradictions, layer mismatches, and unresolved tensions across frameworks, constructs, motifs, or result atoms without averaging them away.
component_programs.summary: A compact index program that packages paradox scanning and contradiction preservation into a reusable analysis pass. It can stand alone or serve as a component program inside larger synthesis workflows.
required_inputs: result atoms or comparable comparative signals
component_programs.notes: Useful both as a standalone analysis program and as a reusable component inside larger synthesis programs such as ILENS or Human Model Card.

canonical_records.short_description: A family of relational frameworks describing recurring patterns of security, anxiety, avoidance, and closeness regulation.
A dimensional trait personality framework typically organized around Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism.
A relational preference framework describing preferred modes of expressing and receiving affection.

motif.name: Affective Reactivity
motif.summary: Sensitivity to stress, threat, volatility, and emotional perturbation.
motif.description: A recurrent motif spanning trait, attachment, shadow, and stress-oriented systems that speak to reactivity, anxiety, emotional load, or instability.

motif.name: Attachment and Closeness Regulation
motif.summary: How a framework encodes safety, proximity, dependence, and distance in close relationships.
motif.description: A relationship-layer motif for security, anxiety, avoidance, availability, reassurance seeking, and closeness management.

motif.name: Exploratory Openness
motif.summary: Appetite for novelty, imagination, curiosity, and experiential exploration.
motif.description: A recurring motif across trait, style, and symbolic systems that captures interest in novelty, complexity, imagination, and expansion beyond routine.

motif.name: Relational Care Signaling
motif.summary: Preferred channels for expressing and receiving care, validation, and recognition.
motif.description: A motif for frameworks that describe how care becomes legible, especially in relational preference systems and practical communication grammars.

motif.name: Social Energy Orientation
motif.summary: How a framework encodes social activation, outward engagement, and inward recharge.
motif.description: A house translation axis for frameworks that speak about extraversion, introversion, social charge, or preferred outward intensity without assuming they all mean the same thing.

relevant_mappings.rationale: Attachment anxiety directly names sensitivity to rejection, abandonment, and reassurance needs in close relationships.
Attachment avoidance directly names distance regulation, intimacy discomfort, and reluctance toward dependence.
Big Five extraversion is one of the clearest direct encodings of outward social activation and engagement in the current corpus.
Neuroticism is one of the strongest direct trait-language anchors for stress sensitivity and negative affect reactivity.
Openness to Experience is one of the strongest direct house anchors for novelty, imagination, and exploratory appetite.
Quality Time expresses relational care through presence and attention rather than through trait or motive description.
Words of Affirmation is not a whole attachment construct, but it is a clear signal about how care and validation become legible.

required_inputs: two explicitly separated stacks or structured result bundles
framework records for any compared systems
declared comparison question or relationship context

execution_order: Resolve canonical framework records for the current target scope.
Trace target frameworks or constructs through the motif layer.
Expand interaction hypotheses relevant to the scoped targets and selected protocol.
Load the protocol's technique bundle and preserve cautions.
Return structured feedback through the preferred research contribution models.

contribution_models.name: Protocol Feedback
contribution_models.purpose: Capture whether a downstream protocol produced useful, misleading, or incomplete synthesis.
contribution_models.privacy_posture: Evaluate the protocol output rather than the person's raw life material.
contribution_models.notes: Keeps downstream promptcraft and runtime behavior connected back to the repository without polluting canonical framework records.
